# 30-Day Posting Queue — built from `assets/content-pack/`

Source of truth: the 12 posts in `assets/content-pack/01–12` (each under 400
chars). **Every post below is copied verbatim from those files — no new posts
were invented.** The 30 days are covered by rotation, not fabrication:

- **Days 1–12 (Cycle 1):** all 12 posts in order, one per day.
- **Days 13–24 (Cycle 2):** the same 12 in a different order, on a different
  platform, with a fresh first-line context where the platform allows it.
  The quoted post body itself is unchanged.
- **Days 25–30 (Encore):** 6 repeats of the most evergreen posts, labeled
  ENCORE. Rule: after Day 24, swap these 6 for your 6 best-performing posts
  (most genuine replies/saves) — same files, your data picks the winners.

## Slot key (suggested starting points, not promises)

These are conventional high-attention windows to start with. They are **not**
performance claims — track your own replies/saves per slot for 30 days, then
keep what works for your audience. All times are the account owner's local time.

| Slot | Window (local) | Default platform |
|------|----------------|------------------|
| S1 | 07:30–08:30 | LinkedIn (pre-work scroll) |
| S2 | 12:00–13:00 | X (lunch scroll) |
| S3 | 17:30–18:30 | Reddit / community replies (after-work browsing) |

## Platform notes

- **X:** post the body as-is (all 12 fit). No hashtag stuffing. Max 1 soft CTA
  per week (see Day 7 note) — otherwise value only.
- **LinkedIn:** you may prepend ONE line of personal context (e.g. "Something
  I enforce on every build:"). The quoted body stays verbatim.
- **Reddit / Discord / Slack:** NEVER top-level-post promos. Only adapt the
  post into a genuine reply where it directly answers someone's question, and
  only in communities where self-promo is allowed. When in doubt, help without
  linking anything.
- **Soft CTA rule (max 1×/week):** append at most: "I put my exact templates
  in a starter kit — DM if curious." Never on Reddit.

---

## Cycle 1 — Days 1–12 (every post once, in order)

### Day 1 — X · S2 · source: `content-pack/01-fixed-vs-hourly.md`

> Fixed pricing beats hourly for small sites. The client knows the total upfront, and you get rewarded for working fast instead of punished. Scope pages + features in writing, include 2 revision rounds, quote extras separately.

### Day 2 — LinkedIn · S1 · source: `content-pack/02-idea-calls.md`

> Free consults attract tire-kickers. I charge $5 for a 60-min idea call: we map pages, features, and content, and the client keeps the plan. Serious people say yes, time-wasters filter themselves. Credited toward the build.

### Day 3 — X · S2 · source: `content-pack/03-personalize-outreach.md`

> Cold outreach works when the first two lines prove you looked. Name one specific thing on their site, suggest one concrete fix, ask one small question. Templates handle structure; specifics earn the reply.

### Day 4 — LinkedIn · S1 · source: `content-pack/04-content-deadlines.md`

> Most web projects stall on content, not code. Set a content deadline in the proposal: who provides text, photos, and logo, and by when. No content, no build start. Say it kindly, enforce it always.

### Day 5 — X · S2 · source: `content-pack/05-revision-limits.md`

> Include 2 revision rounds, defined as one consolidated list each. Drip feedback gets bundled before work starts. Extra rounds are billed at a stated rate. Bounds make clients happier, not stricter.

### Day 6 — Reddit/community reply · S3 · source: `content-pack/06-deposits.md`

> Take 50% before writing code, 50% before launch. Every time. Deposits aren't about trust, they're about sequencing: signed scope plus deposit equals a scheduled build. No deposit, no slot.

(Reply-only: use where someone asks about getting paid / deposits / scope creep. No link, no CTA.)

### Day 7 — LinkedIn · S1 · source: `content-pack/07-handoff-docs.md` · ⚡ CTA week 1 (only CTA this week)

> Ship a handoff doc with every site: hosting logins, deploy steps, how to edit text and images, third-party services. It cuts support messages in half and makes you look like a professional studio of one.

Soft CTA allowed today only: append "I put my exact templates in a starter kit — DM if curious."

### Day 8 — X · S2 · source: `content-pack/08-site-speed.md`

> For local businesses, speed is a feature. Compress images, skip heavy frameworks, keep one clear call-to-action above the fold. A fast one-pager that loads anywhere beats a slow five-pager.

### Day 9 — LinkedIn · S1 · source: `content-pack/09-templates-vs-custom.md`

> Templates are fine until the business outgrows them: slow loads, generic structure, plugin sprawl. Custom pays off when one conversion goal matters — calls, bookings, or quote requests — and someone owns launch end to end.

### Day 10 — X · S2 · source: `content-pack/10-follow-up-once.md`

> After a proposal, follow up exactly once after 4-5 days: ask if it's still a fit or if you should close it out. Polite, short, no chase. Silence is data. Move on to the next 5 pitches.

### Day 11 — Reddit/community reply · S3 · source: `content-pack/11-support-window.md`

> Include a 14-day bug-fix window, then stop free support. Bugs versus the agreed scope are free; changes are quoted. Offer a small monthly plan for updates and monitoring. Boundaries fund longevity.

(Reply-only: use where someone asks about support boundaries / free revisions. No link, no CTA.)

### Day 12 — LinkedIn · S1 · source: `content-pack/12-track-outreach.md`

> Track outreach in a plain spreadsheet: date, prospect, channel, template, reply, call, close. Review weekly. After 50 pitches you'll know which message works. Most beginners quit before the data arrives.

## Tracking sheet (copy into your spreadsheet)

| Day | Posted? (Y/N) | Platform | Replies | Saves/likes | Link clicks | Notes |
|-----|---------------|----------|---------|-------------|-------------|-------|

Review weekly: which 3 posts earned the most genuine replies? Expand those
winners into longer posts or short videos next cycle. All sample time slots
are starting points — keep the slots that correlate with real replies for
your audience; drop the rest. No reach or income is promised anywhere here.
